title: Loss
subtext: A number that measures how wrong a model's prediction is
author: Buzzpy

description.title: Loss
texts: Loss (also called the loss value or cost) is a single number that quantifies the difference between a model's prediction and the correct answer. A lower loss means the model is performing better; a loss of zero would mean perfect predictions.

Different tasks use different loss functions. For regression problems, Mean Squared Error (MSE) is common. For classification, Cross-Entropy Loss is widely used. The choice of loss function directly shapes what the model learns to optimize.

The loss is calculated after every forward pass during training. The backward pass then uses it to compute gradients and update the model's weights — making loss the central signal that drives all learning.
